snapshot.stmt:
The answer is negative for the candidate as defined.  For the realized design \(Z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), put
\[
\rho_n(z)=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha).
\]
For the deterministic regular-regime sequence \(\delta_n\equiv0\), there is a law \(P_0\in\mathcal M\) and a constant \(c_0>0\), depending only on the declared constants, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_0}\rho_n(Z)
=\mathbb E_{P_0}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{Z,x}(t_\alpha)
\geq c_0h_n^\beta,
\qquad
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)
\geq c_0h_n^\beta
=c_0n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{2\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)}{r_n}
\geq 2c_0n^{(\kappa+1)/[2(2\beta+\kappa+1)]}\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
\frac{L_n^\star}{r_n}\leq C.
\]
The worst-case expected full length of an untruncated symmetric interval with realized radius \(\rho_n\) also has the displayed divergent lower bound.  Hence this interval cannot attain a finite, let alone sharp, asymptotic minimax constant uniformly over the regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes.  This counterexample satisfies bounded outcomes and the measurable two-sided polynomial density envelope.  It refutes the combined honesty-and-sharpness question through failure of sharpness; no conclusion about marginal honesty of an otherwise fully specified center is needed.

defs.def:bandwidth: \(h_n=\inf\{h\in(0,1-\bar\delta]:n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h)^\kappa\geq1\}\), with \(h_n=1-\bar\delta\) if the set is empty.
defs.def:exact-modulus-handle:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), a split block \(I_2\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\ell\), \(\beta\), \(\kappa\), \(L\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(p_{\min}\), \(\delta_n\), \(h_n>0\), and a test multiplier \(t\geq0\).  For a realized design \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), put \(u_i=(A_i-\delta_n)/h_n\), \(S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}\), and
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}=\left\{w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}: w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\quad \sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell\right\}.
\]
If \(V_{z,x}\) is the matrix whose row indexed by \(i\in S_{z,x}\) is \(v_\ell(u_i)^\top\), these are equivalently the affine realized-design constraints \(V_{z,x}^\top w_{S_{z,x}}=e_0\), and the associated total Gram is \(G_x=V_{z,x}^\top V_{z,x}\).  Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) that are continuous and satisfy
\[
\left|f(a')-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}f^{(j)}(a)(a'-a)^j/j!\right|\leq L|a'-a|^\beta
\quad\text{for every }a,a'\in[0,1],
\]
where the derivatives are the intrinsic derivatives on \([0,1]\) used in the declared Hölder condition.  For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define the exact realized Hölder bias and conditional radius objective by
\[
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
=\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)\right|,
\qquad
\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w)
=\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)+t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The realized exact modulus is the real-valued totalization
\[
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)=
\begin{cases}
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w),&\mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\
0,&\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus the empty affine-feasible set has value zero, matching the real \(\operatorname{sInf}\) convention in the verified construction.  Define
\[
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t)
=\int \operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes n})(z),
\]
the real-valued integral under the \(n\)-fold independent observed-design law induced by \(P\).  The inputs \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\) enter by requiring that \(P\) satisfy the corresponding member conditions of \(\mathcal M\); they do not impose any additional smoothness on \(\pi_x\).  Finally set
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2},\qquad
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)
=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t_\alpha).
\]
Both \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) and \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) are radius, or half-length, quantities.  An untruncated symmetric interval with such radius has full length twice the radius.  The zero value on \(\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing\) only totalizes this candidate handle on singular designs; no validity, nondegeneracy, honesty, or optimality of an interval using that convention is asserted here.

snapshot.stmt:
Specialize the declared parameter to \(\beta=1\), so that \(\ell=0\), and take \(\delta_n\equiv0\).  For the realized design \(Z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), define
\[
Q_{n,x}(z)=\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha),
\qquad
\rho_n(z)=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}Q_{n,x}(z).
\]
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), the maps \(Q_{n,x}\) and \(\rho_n\) are Borel measurable, hence almost everywhere strongly measurable and integrable under the \(n\)-fold observed-design law, with
\[
0\leq Q_{n,x}(z)\leq Lh_n+t_\alpha,
\qquad
0\leq\rho_n(z)\leq Lh_n+t_\alpha.
\]
Consequently every literal real integral \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) in this specialization is well defined, and the set of integrated handles whose real supremum defines \(\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)\) is nonempty and bounded above.  There are \(P_0\in\mathcal M\), \(x_0\in\mathcal X\), and constants \(c_0>0\) and \(C<\infty\), depending only on the declared constants, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
h_n=n^{-1/(\kappa+3)},
\qquad
\mathbb E_{P_0}\rho_n(Z)\geq
\mathbb E_{P_0}Q_{n,x_0}(Z)\geq c_0h_n,
\qquad
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)\geq c_0h_n.
\]
Since \(r_n=n^{-1/2}\) in this specialization,
\[
\frac{2\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)}{r_n}
\geq2c_0n^{(\kappa+1)/(2(\kappa+3))}\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
\frac{L_n^\star}{r_n}\leq C.
\]
The worst-case expected full length of an untruncated symmetric interval with realized radius \(\rho_n\) has the same divergent lower-order comparison.  Thus the literal zero-totalized real-integral candidate cannot furnish a single sharp asymptotic minimax-constant theorem uniformly over the full declared \(\beta\)-range and all threshold regimes.  This result does not decide marginal honesty, sharpness for any separately fixed \(\beta>1\), or the general exact minimax constant.
